x-e-e1-01.title: Find the actions that don't match the pool notice
x-e-e1-01.topic: Short greetings, notices, and pictures drawn in words
x-e-e1-01.goal: Match the three rules on the notice to each person's situation, choose the cases that break the rules, and say the reason in English.
x-e-e1-01.material:
The notice at the pool entrance (written in words only, no picture):

Pool Rules
1. No running.
2. Swim caps on, please.
3. Under 8? Come with a grown-up.

(grown-up = an adult)

Four people are going to the pool.
Mina is 7. She comes with her mom, and she has a cap.
Jun is 10. He comes alone, and he has no cap.
Tom is 6. He comes with his brother. His brother is 9. Tom has a cap.
Sue is 11. She walks to the pool alone, and she has a cap.
x-e-e1-01.thinking.0: Apply the rules to each person separately
x-e-e1-01.thinking.2: Tell someone in English, giving evidence
x-e-e1-01.prereq.1: Easy pronouns like I, you, he, she
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose everyone who breaks the rules on the notice.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.hint.0: Make a table with each person's age, who they came with, and cap, one by one.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.hint.1: Find which information each rule pairs with, and connect them with lines.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.r.a: Check whether you matched Mina's age and who she came with against rule 3.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.r.b: Match rule 2 with what Jun has.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.r.c: Think about whether the person who came with Tom is the same as the person the rule talks about.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.r.d: Match Sue's age and the way she walks against rules 1 and 3 separately.
x-e-e1-01.s.s1.explain: Jun has no cap, so he breaks rule 2. Tom is under 8, but the brother who came with him is 9, so he is not a 'grown-up', and Tom breaks rule 3. Mina came with her mom, and Sue is 11, so it is fine for her to walk and come alone.
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.prompt: Tell Tom's brother in one or two sentences in English. Connect to the rule the reason Tom can't go into the pool now.
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.hint.0: First compare Tom's age with the number in rule 3.
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.hint.1: Start with 'Tom is under 8, so ...' and write what is needed after it.
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you connect why Tom can't go in to the rule (under 8)?
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you say why his brother is not a grown-up?
x-e-e1-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Are your English sentences short and easy to understand?

x-e-e1-02.title: Fix the wrong line in a copied lost-and-found notice
x-e-e1-02.topic: Short greetings, notices, and pictures drawn in words
x-e-e1-02.goal: Compare a lost-and-found notice with a message a friend copied from it, line by line, find the wrong line, and rewrite it correctly.
x-e-e1-02.material:
A notice on the school bulletin board (written in words only):

Lost and Found
Found: a blue water bottle, near Room 3.
Ask Ms. Park in Room 1 after school.

Your friend Jia saw this notice because she was looking for her water bottle, and sent a message to Hana. Hana wants to compare it with the notice.
x-e-e1-02.thinking.0: Compare the original and the copy line by line
x-e-e1-02.thinking.2: Write the corrected sentence in English
x-e-e1-02.prereq.1: Reading room numbers like Room 1, Room 3
x-e-e1-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line in Jia's message that is different from the notice.
x-e-e1-02.s.s1.hint.0: Point to the words in the notice (color, room number, person's name) one by one and match them with the lines of the message.
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.hint.0: Reread the line in the notice that starts with 'Ask'.
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.hint.1: There is only one word to change in the original sentence. Find where that word is.
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you check in the notice the room number where Ms. Park is?
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you tell apart the place where the bottle was found (Room 3) and the place to ask (Room 1)?
x-e-e1-02.s.s1.hint.1: For each line of the message, match it to the line of the notice it copies, and look for a word that does not match.
x-e-e1-02.s.s1.explain: Line 4 is wrong. In the notice, Ms. Park is in Room 1, but the message says Room 3, so it is wrong. The blue in line 2 is the same as in the notice, and the Room 3 in line 3 is where the bottle was found, so it is correct.
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.prompt: Fix the wrong line you just found so that it matches the notice, and write it in English.
x-e-e1-02.s.s2.placeholder: Write the corrected sentence in English.

x-e-e1-03.title: Make a two-line notice to post on the classroom door
x-e-e1-03.topic: Short greetings, notices, and pictures drawn in words
x-e-e1-03.goal: Judge what information (where, when) the reader of a notice needs, choose a suitable notice, and write your own two-line notice.
x-e-e1-03.material: The students of Class 3 are in the music room from 10:00 to 11:00 today. They want to post a notice on the classroom door. A visitor who comes to the Class 3 classroom at 10:30 will read this notice.
x-e-e1-03.thinking.0: Think about the information the reader needs
x-e-e1-03.prereq.0: Easy words like music room, today
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the notice that lets a visitor who comes at 10:30 know both 'where to go' and 'how long to wait'.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.hint.0: First write two questions a visitor would want to ask.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.hint.1: Mark one by one whether each notice answers those two questions.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.r.b: Think about whether you can tell how long 'later' is.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.r.c: Check whether this notice says both things the visitor wants to know.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.r.d: Check whether it has only a start time, or also an end time.
x-e-e1-03.s.s1.explain: c tells both the place (music room) and the end time (11:00). In a the place is missing, in b how long is missing, and in d the end time is missing.
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.prompt: Write a notice in English, in two lines, to post on the Class 3 classroom door. It must include the place and until what time.
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.hint.0: First write one word each for where, when, and who.
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.hint.1: Write 'where' on the first line and 'when' on the second line, then revise.
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you put only the needed information in the two lines?
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can someone passing by read it and tell where, and until what time?
x-e-e1-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you choose some more information you want to add (e.g., Class 3, Please wait)? (Optional)

x-e-e1-04.title: Who is the speaker? Changing your thinking as clues increase
x-e-e1-04.topic: Clues about who, what, and where
x-e-e1-04.goal: Each time a line of speech adds a clue, judge again who the speaker is, and explain the deciding clue in English.
x-e-e1-04.material: You will see the lines a person says, one line at a time. Follow the clues and think about who the speaker is.
x-e-e1-04.thinking.0: Keep several possibilities open from one clue
x-e-e1-04.thinking.1: Revise your judgment with a new clue
x-e-e1-04.prereq.0: Easy words like book, card, week
x-e-e1-04.prereq.1: Greetings like Welcome, Can I help you?
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.prompt: The lines come out one by one. Each time, choose all the people who could be the speaker.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.hint.0: Of the people you left in the previous step, only check again whether they fit the new line.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.hint.1: In the new line, find the words that name an 'object' or a 'period of time'.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: Looking at this one line only, who could be the speaker?
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.after: From the first line alone, several people are possible, such as a store clerk or a librarian.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: People in stores also give this kind of greeting.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Think about whether this greeting is often used on a bus.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: People in libraries also ask words offering help.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: People in shops that sell books also give the same greeting.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: Putting the two lines together, who is possible?
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.after: Books came up, so the clothes shop clerk and the bus driver dropped out. The librarian and the bookshop clerk remain.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Think about whether it fits with books coming up.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Think about whether it connects to books.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: It could be a person at a place with books.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: It could be a person at a shop with books.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: Putting all three lines together, who fits best?
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Since the speaker asks to see a card and says you may keep the book for two weeks, it is most likely a librarian who lends books. At a bookshop, when you buy a book there is usually no time period.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Check whether it fits the new clue.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Think about what 'two weeks' and 'card' would mean at a bookshop.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Check whether it fits the new clue.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Think about what the words card and two weeks do.
x-e-e1-04.s.s1.reflect: If you settled on one person from the first line only, look back at how your thinking changed as new clues came out. The possibilities got smaller with each clue.
x-e-e1-04.s.s2.prompt: Write in English one clue in the last line that makes you think 'librarian' rather than 'bookshop clerk'.
x-e-e1-04.s.s2.hint.0: In the last line, find a word that would be used differently at a bookshop and at a library.
x-e-e1-04.s.s2.hint.1: Write one sentence in the form: '__ means ~, so ...'.
x-e-e1-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you say that the clue you chose really separates a bookshop from a library?
x-e-e1-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you explain what 'card' or 'two weeks' does?

x-e-e1-05.title: A cinema or a train station? Comparing the strength of clues
x-e-e1-05.topic: Clues about who, what, and where
x-e-e1-05.goal: Compare how strongly the clues in a conversation decide the place, and explain in English why weak clues alone are not enough.
x-e-e1-05.material:
Two people talk like this.
A: Two tickets, please.
B: Which film?
A: The 3 o'clock one.
B: Row F or Row G?
A: Row F, please.

(Row = a line of seats, film = a movie)

Your friend Yuna says, "Tickets! It's a train station." Your friend Min says, "It's a cinema (a movie theater)."
x-e-e1-05.thinking.1: Know that one clue can fit several places
x-e-e1-05.thinking.2: Answer a friend's claim with evidence
x-e-e1-05.prereq.0: Easy words like ticket, film, seat
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the clues that most strongly support Min's statement ('cinema').
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.hint.0: Test each clue with 'Could it be used at other places too?'
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.hint.1: Imagine saying the same words at a train station or a zoo.
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.r.a: Think about whether a cinema is the only place that needs a ticket.
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.r.b: Think about which place the word film belongs to.
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.r.c: Think about whether a cinema is the only place where times come up.
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.r.d: Think about what the row and the letter decide.
x-e-e1-05.s.s1.explain: Film (a movie) and Row F/G (a line of seats) are strong clues pointing to a cinema. Ticket and 3 o'clock are weak clues that can also be used at a train station, a zoo, or a concert hall.
x-e-e1-05.s.s2.prompt: Answer Yuna in English in one or two sentences. Write why 'tickets' alone can't decide that it is a train station.
x-e-e1-05.s.s2.hint.0: Think of two or three other places that use 'ticket'.
x-e-e1-05.s.s2.hint.1: Try starting in the form 'Tickets can be for ... too.'
x-e-e1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you name at least one other place where tickets are used?
x-e-e1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you mention the clues pointing to a cinema (film, Row)?

x-e-e1-06.title: A mystery object: what should we ask next?
x-e-e1-06.topic: Clues about who, what, and where
x-e-e1-06.goal: With several candidates left, choose the question that best separates the candidates, and make your own English question.
x-e-e1-06.material:
A friend is thinking of an object. There are two hints.
Hint 1: It is round. (It is round and roundish)
Hint 2: It is in the kitchen. (It is in the kitchen)

There are four candidates: apple, plate, clock, and cup. You want to find the one by asking yes/no questions.
x-e-e1-06.prereq.0: Question forms like Is it ...? Can you ...?
x-e-e1-06.prereq.1: The words apple, plate, clock, cup
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.prompt: Which question narrows down the candidates best as the next question?
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.hint.0: A question that asks the same thing as a hint you already know can't narrow the candidates.
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.hint.1: Write down which candidates remain when the answer is 'yes' and when it is 'no'.
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.hint.0: Write a line for each of the four candidates' features (eaten, tells the time, holds things).
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.hint.1: Choose a feature that is 'yes' for only one of them and turn it into a question.
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Does it tell the time? If yes, ...
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you avoid asking again about information you already know (round, kitchen)?
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Are the candidates that remain different for 'yes' and for 'no'?
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.r.a: Check whether any of the four candidates would get a different answer.
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.r.b: Check whether you already learned this from Hint 1.
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.r.c: Check whether you already learned this from Hint 2.
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.r.d: Think about whether the answer would split the four candidates.
x-e-e1-06.s.s1.explain: Only the apple can be eaten; the plate, clock, and cup cannot. So "Can you eat it?" splits the candidates. "Round" and "kitchen" are already known from the hints, and "nice" differs from person to person, so it cannot split the candidates.
x-e-e1-06.s.s2.prompt: Using a different question from the one you chose before, write one English question that can narrow down the candidates, and add in English which candidate is left if the answer is "yes."

x-e-e1-07.title: Find and fix the answer that doesn't fit in a birthday dialogue
x-e-e1-07.goal: Using the situation (whose birthday it is), find the answer in the dialogue that doesn't fit, and choose a fitting answer.
x-e-e1-07.material: Today is Ana's birthday. It is not Leo's birthday. Leo gives Ana a present.
x-e-e1-07.thinking.0: Match the situation and the answers
x-e-e1-07.thinking.1: Find the line that doesn't fit
x-e-e1-07.prereq.0: The expressions Happy birthday, Thank you, You're welcome
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.hint.0: First turn the words into Korean to see in what situation they are used.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.hint.1: Put the choice into line 2 and read whether it connects with Leo's words in the last line.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.r.a: These words answer a thank-you. Who should be giving thanks right now?
x-e-e1-07.s.s1.prompt: In this conversation, choose the line where Ana's answer does not fit the situation.
x-e-e1-07.s.s1.hint.0: First check whose birthday it is today, then read each of Ana's two answers together with what Leo said right before it.
x-e-e1-07.s.s1.hint.1: Check, one line at a time, whether each line can be read as a natural reaction to the line right before it.
x-e-e1-07.s.s1.explain: Line 2 does not fit. Today is Ana's birthday, not Leo's, so "to you too" does not fit. Ana, who received a gift, should say thank you, and then it also connects to Leo's "You're welcome." in the next line.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.prompt: Choose the right answer for Ana in the line you just found.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.r.b: Check whether "me too" fits what Leo said.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.r.c: Think about whether this is a fitting reaction when you receive a gift.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.r.d: Think about who did what for whom at the moment the gift was given.
x-e-e1-07.s.s2.explain: Since she received a gift, Thank you fits. With this fix, Leo's "You're welcome." in the next line also follows naturally.

x-e-e1-08.title: Refusing in different ways to a teacher and a friend
x-e-e1-08.goal: In the same situation (not able to help), judge the tone and information that fit a teacher and a friend, and answer each in English.
x-e-e1-08.material: After class, the teacher says, "Can you help me carry the books?" But you can't help because you have to go to the dentist at 3. It is the same later if a friend says, "Can you help me carry the books?"
x-e-e1-08.thinking.0: Choose words according to the person
x-e-e1-08.thinking.1: Say the refusal and the reason together
x-e-e1-08.thinking.2: Change the same content in a different way
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.prompt: Which is the most fitting answer to the teacher?
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.hint.0: First check whether the words match the situation (the dentist appointment).
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.r.a: Check whether the facts match the situation.
x-e-e1-08.s.s2.prompt: Answer the teacher in English. It must include the words saying you can't help, the reason, and a polite phrase.
x-e-e1-08.s.s2.hint.0: First write the three pieces 'I'm sorry', 'I can't help', and 'I'm going to the dentist' in Korean.
x-e-e1-08.s.s2.hint.1: Connect the three pieces in order into one or two English sentences.
x-e-e1-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Are the refusal, the reason, and politeness all there?
x-e-e1-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Does it sound like the way you talk to a teacher?
x-e-e1-08.s.s3.prompt: Write in English a short answer to give a friend who asks the same favor. Write in a more casual tone than what you said to the teacher, but include the refusal and the reason.
x-e-e1-08.s.s3.hint.0: Keep only the words that are really needed from what you said to the teacher.
x-e-e1-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you write it more casually and shorter than what you wrote to the teacher?
x-e-e1-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Do the refusal and the reason still remain?
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.hint.1: For each answer, mark whether it has all three things (a refusal, a reason, and a tone) and compare them.
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.r.b: It has a reason, but think about whether the tone is suitable for speaking to a teacher.
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.r.c: It is polite, but check whether it includes a reason for refusing.
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.r.d: Check whether it only refuses, or whether it has both a reason and politeness.
x-e-e1-08.s.s1.explain: To a teacher, it is right to say you are sorry and also give a reason. a does not match the facts. b has a reason but the tone is rough, and c is polite but has no reason.

x-e-e1-09.title: Find the missing information in a meeting message and ask about it
x-e-e1-09.topic: Missing information in a two-line message
x-e-e1-09.goal: Judge that you can't meet from a two-line message alone, choose the information you must ask about, and make English questions.
x-e-e1-09.material:
Jisu sent a message.
"Let's play soccer on Saturday. Meet me at the park."

There are two parks near the school, Sun Park and Lake Park. Jisu did not say which park.
x-e-e1-09.thinking.0: Find the information missing from the message
x-e-e1-09.thinking.1: Tell apart information that is really needed and information that is less needed
x-e-e1-09.prereq.0: Question words like what time, which, where
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose everything you can't tell from Jisu's message alone and must ask about in order to meet.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.hint.0: To meet, you need 'when and where'. Check whether the message tells both.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.hint.1: Reread the second sentence of the passage (two parks).
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.r.a: Look at the passage again for how many parks there are.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.o.b: Which month and day Saturday is
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.r.b: Think about whether you can meet without this information.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.r.c: Look for whether the message has a time.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.r.d: Think about whether this is information you must have when trying to meet.
x-e-e1-09.s.s1.explain: The message has no meeting time, and there are two parks, so you can't tell which one. So you need to ask about the time and the place (which park). The date is enough as Saturday, and whether Jisu likes soccer is not information you must have to meet.
x-e-e1-09.s.s2.prompt: Write two questions to Jisu in English. Ask about the time and the park separately.
x-e-e1-09.s.s2.hint.0: Remember that two pieces of information are missing and write two questions.
x-e-e1-09.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Do the two questions ask about different information?
x-e-e1-09.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Are the questions made up of a question mark and a question word?

x-e-e1-10.title: Complete a 'I'll be late' message so Mom isn't worried
x-e-e1-10.topic: Missing information in a two-line message
x-e-e1-10.goal: Find the information missing from a one-line message and write your own two-line message that tells Mom so she won't worry.
x-e-e1-10.material: After school, you will go to the music club and probably get home late. You want to send a text message to your mom. What Mom wants to know is 'what time you will come home' and 'where you are and what you are doing.'
x-e-e1-10.thinking.0: Think about what the receiver wonders
x-e-e1-10.prereq.0: Sentences like I'll be home at 5.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.prompt: Which message tells both things so that Mom feels reassured?
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.hint.0: Write down Mom's two questions and mark whether each message answers them.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.hint.1: Tell apart whether 'late' or 'don't worry' is information or just words to calm feelings.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.r.a: Check whether there is a time.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.r.b: Check one by one whether it answers the two things Mom wonders about.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.r.c: Check whether it has the information 'when you will come'.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.r.d: Check whether it has 'where and what you are doing'.
x-e-e1-10.s.s1.explain: b tells both the time you will come home (5 o'clock) and where you are and what you are doing (music club). The others are missing one of the two.
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.prompt: Write a two-line message to Mom in English. It must include what time you will come home and where (or why) you will be late. You may choose the time freely.
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.hint.0: First write in Korean the two things Mom would want to ask.
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.hint.1: Write the first line as the words about being late and the reason, and the second line as the arrival time.
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.placeholder:
Example: Mom, I'll be late today.
I'm at ... and I'll be home at ...
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can Mom tell what time you will come?
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Can she tell where you are and what you are doing (why you are late)?
x-e-e1-10.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you put only the needed information in the two lines?
